root.name: Indian Defense: Dzindzi-Indian Defense
root.moves: 1. d4 Nf6 2. c4 e6 3. Nf3 a6

overview: Black plays 3...a6 after 1.d4 Nf6 2.c4 e6 3.Nf3, a waiting move that keeps the choice between ...d5, ...c5, ...b5 and a Queen's Indian-like set-up. After 4.Nc3 Black often plays 4...c5 reaching Benoni-style structures. I am less sure of the exact theory; it is a flexible, rarely seen line.

white_ideas.idea: Play Nc3, e4 and d5 for a central grip
Keep pieces flexible and wait for Black's structure

black_ideas.idea: Prepare ...b5 or ...c5 with ...a6 as a useful waiting move
Reach a Benoni or Queen's Gambit set-up favourably

typical_structures.structure: Benoni-like pawn structure after ...c5 and d5

character.notes: Flexible set-up; neither side is forced into sharp play.

approach.notes: A rare side line by Dzindzichashvili; strong players seldom choose it.

level.notes: Needs to know which structure to head for.

character.reason: Waiting move leads to flexible, even positions.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided at move 3.

level.reason: Needs structural understanding rather than memory.
